newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman freezes ties with Israel over settlements.
newsitem.headline: Oman freezes ties with Israel over settlements.

text.p: The Gulf Arab state of Oman said on Sunday it had frozen ties with Israel over the Jewish state's settlement policies, Oman's official news agency ONA reported.

It quoted Oman's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah as saying Oman could not develop ties with the Israeli government "as long as it continued to violate peace agreements" signed with the Palestinians.
Speaking to ONA at a summit of the Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC) in Islamabad, he described Omani ties with Israel as "frozen" in light of tensions in the Middle East.

Israeli-Palestinian tension has been high since right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sent bulldozers last Tuesday to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a new Jewish settlement in territory occupied by Israel.
A suicide bombing, claimed by the radical Moslem Hamas group, killed three Israeli women in Tel Aviv on Friday.
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf Arab states in establishing economic ties with Israel after the Jewish state signed a peace deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation in 1993.
Muscat has in the past frozen commercial ties with Israel and called on it to adhere to previous commitments to the Palestinian leadership.
